about: Real recordings of token streams, made on 2026-11-11 by record-traces.mjs with engine/routes/ollama.js (the route adapter this page runs in the browser). Machine: a laptop with an NVIDIA RTX 3500 Ada Laptop GPU (12 GB), Windows 11, shared with other work while recording. t is milliseconds since the request was sent, on performance.now(). final holds the server's own counters, durations in nanoseconds. The model text is verbatim and unedited. The public-oneshot entry was timed with curl, not with the route adapter.

schema.chunks: [t_ms, kind, text], kind a = answer, t = thinking
schema.placement: from /api/ps after the run: bytes total, bytes in GPU memory, context window
schema.contention: a second request on the same server, its start and end on this trace's clock

traces.label: gpt-oss-20b via the public route, one reply
traces.promptPreview: In three sentences, explain what a token is to a language model.
traces.reasoning:
The user asks: "In three sentences, explain what a token is to a language model." Likely a short explanation. Should be in plain language? It's simple. We must obey system instructions: no overly formal language, no moral phrases, etc. In three sentences.

We should be concise. Probably: a token is a unit of input or output, e.g., words or subwords. For a language model it maps to embeddings. And tokenization process. Let's produce.
chunks: A token is the smallest chunk of text a language model actually processes—often a word, part of a word, or even punctuation, depending on how the model’s tokenizer is set up. Each token gets turned into a numeric vector (an embedding) that the model uses to understand and predict language. When the model runs, it reads a sequence of these tokens, works on them internally, and outputs another sequence of tokens that it expects will be correct text.
traces.note: Non-streamed: the whole reply arrived in one response after 5.91 s. The route reported 322 prompt tokens for a one-line question, so it adds a prompt of its own that the caller never sees.
